original_question: If SK_1(A tensor_F L) vanishes for every field extension L/F, must the index of the central simple algebra A be square-free?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 11.4 (Suslin) in Section 11.B, "SK1 of central simple algebras," stated as the converse to Wang's square-free-index vanishing result for SK1.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact implication in the paper: vanishing of SK1(A tensor_F L) for every field extension L/F, and the conclusion that the index of A should be square-free. It is very close to the paper's official formulation.
missing_details: State explicitly that F is a field and A is a central simple F-algebra.
Define SK1(B) as SL1(B)/[B^x,B^x], where SL1(B) consists of the reduced-norm-1 elements of B.
Clarify that L/F ranges over all field extensions, with no finiteness or separability hypothesis.
Define ind(A) as the degree of the division algebra Brauer-equivalent to A.
Make explicit that the hypothesis is applied to the base change A tensor_F L, viewed as a central simple L-algebra.
Note the paper's intended context: this is Suslin's conjectural converse to Wang's theorem that SK1(A)=0 when ind(A) is square-free.
refined_question: Let F be a field and let A be a central simple F-algebra. For each field extension L/F, write SK1(A tensor_F L) := SL1(A tensor_F L)/[(A tensor_F L)^x,(A tensor_F L)^x], where SL1 denotes the reduced-norm-1 subgroup. If SK1(A tensor_F L)=0 for every field extension L/F, must ind(A), the degree of the division algebra Brauer-equivalent to A, be square-free?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Theorem 11.3: let F be a field and A a central simple F-algebra. If the linear algebraic group SL_r(A) is retract rational for some (equivalently, every) integer r >= 2, must ind(A) be square-free?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 11.B rather than the earlier crossed-product problems. In that subsection the paper first defines SK1 for a central simple F-algebra, recalls that Wang proved SK1(A)=0 when ind(A) is square-free, and then states Suslin's conjecture exactly as the converse implication your draft asks about. Theorem 11.3 in the same subsection is the paper's explicit equivalent reformulation, relating vanishing of SK1(A tensor_F L) for all field extensions L/F to retract rationality of SL_r(A).

citations.label: opening definition of SK1 of central simple algebras
